$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Cloud Monitoring. One entry per console section; level per substrate (nano = shared core, also dev_server/unified ingress; offline = appliance). Proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py. GCP probes speak REST, not the AWS probe helper, so claims lean on `tests` (the core's own conformance suite) instead of `probe`.

gcp.monitoring.alert-policy.crud.title: Alerting policies (create, list, get, patch, delete)

gcp.monitoring.notification-channels.title: Notification channels (email, SMS, Slack, PagerDuty, Pub/Sub, webhooks)
limitations: Channels are created, verified and attached to policies for real, but Vyomi never actually sends an email/SMS/Slack message/webhook call when an alert would fire — there is no outbound delivery path.

gcp.monitoring.incidents.title: Alerts (open incidents)
limitations: Vyomi's alert-evaluation engine evaluates condition_threshold and condition_absent conditions for real against the stored time series a policy's filter matches, opening and closing incidents (and honoring active snoozes) exactly like the real engine — there is no public incidents.list API, so this is modeled on the documented webhook notification payload shape (incident_id/state/started_at/ended_at/...) instead. condition_matched_log, MQL (condition_monitoring_query_language) and PromQL (condition_prometheus_query_language) conditions are never evaluated (no log ingestion or query-language engine), so policies that rely solely on those never open an incident. Multi-condition policies are tracked as one whole-policy incident rather than per matching resource (AND_WITH_MATCHING_RESOURCE doesn't cross-match resources between conditions).

gcp.monitoring.uptime-checks.config.title: Uptime check configuration (create, list, patch, delete)
limitations: Checks are validated and stored exactly like the real UptimeCheckConfigs API, including per-region selection, but Vyomi never dispatches an actual HTTP/HTTPS/TCP probe from any region — there is no pass/fail result to report per-region.

gcp.monitoring.uptime-checks.probing.title: Uptime check results (pass/fail per region)
limitations: Vyomi never dispatches the configured probe from any region, so there is no real up/down result to report — configured checks are never shown as failing.

gcp.monitoring.synthetic-monitors.title: Synthetic monitors
limitations: A synthetic monitor is a real UptimeCheckConfig whose check type is synthetic_monitor (a Cloud Functions v2 target) instead of http_check/tcp_check — it's created, listed and deleted for real. Vyomi has no Cloud Functions execution runtime, so a monitor's run status, success rate and average latency are never populated.

gcp.monitoring.slos.title: Services & SLOs
limitations: Services and their SLOs (goal, compliance period, indicator) are real resources — the same Service Monitoring API v3 create/get/list/delete the gcloud/client libraries use. For a request-based SLO (service_level_indicator.request_based.good_total_ratio), Vyomi computes a real error-budget fraction from the good/total time series you've written, via the same select_slo_compliance()/select_slo_budget_fraction()/select_slo_health() timeSeries.list filter functions the real API reserves for SLO burn-down queries — the 'SLOs out of error budget' count reflects that. Windows-based and basic SLIs aren't evaluated (shown as '—', since there's no live request/latency pipeline to classify them against). 'SLOs with firing alert' is always 0: an SLO's burn-rate alert condition is a condition_monitoring_query_language (MQL) alert condition, and Vyomi's alert-evaluation engine (see gcp.monitoring.incidents) only evaluates condition_threshold/condition_absent, so a burn-rate condition never actually opens an incident.

gcp.monitoring.metric-descriptors.title: Metric and monitored-resource descriptors (built-in catalog + custom metrics)

gcp.monitoring.metrics-explorer.title: Metrics Explorer (query time series: filter, align, reduce)
limitations: The Builder query mode runs against real stored time series (write, filter, per-series alignment, cross-series reduction). PromQL query mode is not parsed — switch to Builder to run a query.

gcp.monitoring.dashboards.crud.title: Custom dashboards (create, list, get, patch, delete)
limitations: A dashboard's name, labels and layout are stored and returned exactly as the real Dashboards API (v1) would, round-tripping through etag-checked updates. Tiles built with a classic timeSeriesFilter query render a real chart from live stored time series in the dashboard builder; tiles using MQL (timeSeriesQueryLanguage) are not parsed, matching the Metrics Explorer PromQL gap.

gcp.monitoring.metrics-management.title: Metrics Management (billable volume, reads, cardinality per metric)
limitations: The metric catalog itself (type, domain, labels, referencing alert policies) is real, from the same metricDescriptors.list every SDK calls. Billable byte/sample volume, 30-day read counts, custom-dashboard references and label cardinality come from Google's internal billing and usage pipelines, not the Monitoring API — Vyomi has no usage/billing meter for ingested time series, so those columns are always empty. Excluding a metric isn't modeled either; it's a console-only feature with no public API.

gcp.monitoring.integrations.title: Integrations catalog
limitations: The catalog itself (which platforms are available, their type/platform metadata) is reference data, the same on every project, not a simulated resource. Installing one is real: it creates a Dashboards API (v1) dashboard in this project with a tile wired to a real metric filter for that platform, via the same create call the Dashboards page uses. The curated alerting policies a real install also adds aren't modeled, and the catalog's Status filter (installed/not installed) isn't wired up.

gcp.monitoring.permissions.title: Permissions (project IAM bindings)
limitations: Grant/Remove access calls the real resourcemanager-style projects.getIamPolicy/setIamPolicy round-trip (the same generic IAM policy store every Vyomi GCP resource uses). Vyomi stores and lists the bindings exactly as granted, but never evaluates them — holding (or lacking) a Monitoring role doesn't actually gate any Monitoring API call.

gcp.monitoring.cost-explorer.title: Cost Explorer
limitations: Cost Explorer reads from Cloud Billing export data, a separate product Vyomi doesn't simulate.

gcp.monitoring.trace-explorer.title: Trace explorer
limitations: Distributed tracing (Cloud Trace) ingestion and the trace explorer UI are a separate product from Cloud Monitoring; Vyomi doesn't model span ingestion.

gcp.monitoring.error-reporting.title: Error reporting
limitations: Error Reporting groups errors parsed out of Cloud Logging entries into deduplicated signatures with occurrence counts and charts. Vyomi has no log-based error grouping, so this shows the real ERROR-and-above severity entries from Cloud Logging (the same entries:list API) as a flat, ungrouped list instead.

gcp.monitoring.application-monitoring.title: Application monitoring (APM)
limitations: Application monitoring needs Cloud Profiler/APM language agents reporting into the project; Vyomi has no application runtime to instrument. The alert policy wizard's Application and Service or Workload selectors, which link a policy to Application Monitoring, aren't modeled either.

gcp.monitoring.ops-agent.title: VMs with Ops Agent
limitations: Ops Agent inventory comes from Compute Engine VMs reporting a running agent. Vyomi doesn't model Compute Engine instances or agent check-ins.

gcp.monitoring.settings.log-scopes.title: Log scopes / Metric scope / Trace scopes (Settings tabs)
limitations: Scopes link a monitoring workspace to other projects' logs/metrics/traces for multi-project observability. Vyomi is single-project and doesn't model cross-project scoping.
